qt: to the Commission Manu Pineda (The Left) Subject:

In 2018, the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child warned Spain about the participation of children in bullfighting. At present, girls and boys over the age of 14 can attend so-called ‘practical lessons’, in which sharp objects are used on animals. The children could injure or harm themselves with these objects, or even be killed. As part of these activities, children also witness violent acts, normalising this kind of behaviour. Some local action groups receiving European funding are promoting these classes. Other actors have used the EAFRD programme to subsidise the creation of a bullfighting school. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider that these events are in line with the EU strategy on the rights of children and adolescents?
How does the Commission view the use of EU-affiliated funds or resources for such activities?
Will the Commission recommend additional measures to ensure that children do not participate in such activities?

to the Commission Ana Miranda (Verts/ALE) (12 March 2024) Subject: Free access for children to an activity involving animal cruelty In 2018, the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child warned the Spanish state about the participation of children in bullfighting. In 2023, it passed General Comment No 26, in which it calls for children to be protected from exposure to all forms of violence, including violence inflicted on animals. Valencia Provincial Council organises a ‘children’s area’ which children of any age can access free of charge and unaccompanied by their families. In the area, they can witness animal cruelty and injured people, such as participants in the event themselves (1). In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider that these events are in line with the EU strategy on the rights of children and adolescents?
Does the Commission intend to make recommendations in this regard to comply with the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
Is the Commission aware that, according to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child recommendations, children’s fundamental rights are being breached?

Joint answer given by Vice-President Šuica on behalf of the European Commission (28 May 2024) The rights of the child are enshrined in Article 24 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (Charter) (2). The EU strategy on the rights of the child (3) aims, among others, to combat violence against children and ensure child protection. Member States must respect the values enshrined in Article 2 of Treaty on the European Union and the Charter when implementing the Union budget. Therefore, when a Member State receives funding from Union programmes such as the EAFRD it has an obligation to respect the rights enshrined in the Charter, including Article 24. The Financial Regulation recast, planned to entry into force in autumn 2024, will introduce a further reference to respect of EU values and the Charter when Member States implement the Union budget. Likewise, on agricultural funds, Member States shall design the interventions of their CAP (5) Strategic Plans in accordance with the Charter. Leader Local Action Groups design and implement local development strategies according to development needs analysis and potential of the area, with the involvement of local population, and the proposed projects of these strategies should contribute to one or more CAP specific objectives, particularly number 8 (6). In a situation where Member States are not using EU funding for such activities, it is for their authorities, including their judicial authorities, to ensure that fundamental rights are effectively respected and protected in accordance with their national legislation and international human rights obligations, including the the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
